LRU Cache — Implement from Scratch

Least Recently Used — evicts the item not accessed for the longest time. HashMap + Doubly Linked List = O(1) for both get and put. The #1 most asked cache question across Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Apple (~30% of interviews). LeetCode #146.
Medium LeetCode #146 Amazon · Google · Meta · Microsoft · Apple
get() O(1) put() O(1) Space O(capacity)

1

Core Idea

What is LRU?

A fixed-capacity cache that, when full, evicts the least recently used entry — the one that hasn't been read or written for the longest time.

Every get() and put() marks the key as "most recently used".

Why build from scratch?

  • Tests understanding of HashMap + Doubly Linked List synergy
  • O(1) for both operations — interviewers want to see you achieve this
  • LinkedHashMap does it built-in, but interviewers want the manual version
2

Data Structure — HashMap + Doubly Linked List

HashMap
key → Node
O(1) lookup
Doubly Linked List
access order
HEAD = most recent
O(1) + O(1)
both ops
constant time
Why dummy head & tail? They eliminate null checks — real nodes always sit between them. We never remove the sentinels.
Why doubly linked? Need O(1) removal of any node. With a doubly linked list + direct reference from HashMap, you can unlink a node by updating prev.next and next.prev — no traversal needed. A singly linked list would need O(n) to find the previous node.
3

Operations — Step by Step

get(key)

  1. Look up key in HashMap → O(1)
  2. If miss → return -1
  3. If hit → remove node from current position
  4. Re-insert node right after HEAD (most recent)
  5. Return value

put(key, value)

  1. If key exists → update value, move to HEAD
  2. If cache full → remove TAIL.prev (LRU node), remove from HashMap
  3. Create new Node(key, value)
  4. Insert right after HEAD
  5. Add to HashMap: key → node

Node — Doubly Linked List

inner class

Each node stores key + value + prev/next pointers. Key is stored so that during eviction from the tail, we can also remove the entry from the HashMap.

private static class Node {
    int key;
    int value;
    Node prev;
    Node next;

    Node(int key, int value) {
        this.key = key;
        this.value = value;
    }
}
2

Fields & Constructor

cache setup
private final int capacity;
private final Map<Integer, Node> map;   // key → Node (O(1) lookup)
private final Node head;                 // dummy head (most recent side)
private final Node tail;                 // dummy tail (least recent side)

public LRUCache(int capacity) {
    this.capacity = capacity;
    this.map = new HashMap<>();
    this.head = new Node(-1, -1);
    this.tail = new Node(-1, -1);
    head.next = tail;
    tail.prev = head;
}
3

get(key) — O(1)

read path
public int get(int key) {
    if (!map.containsKey(key)) {
        return -1;  // cache miss
    }
    Node node = map.get(key);
    removeNode(node);       // detach from current position
    addToHead(node);        // attach right after head (most recent)
    return node.value;
}
4

put(key, value) — O(1)

write path
public void put(int key, int value) {
    // Case 1: Key already exists → update + move to head
    if (map.containsKey(key)) {
        Node node = map.get(key);
        node.value = value;
        removeNode(node);
        addToHead(node);
        return;
    }
    // Case 2: Cache is full → evict LRU (tail.prev)
    if (map.size() == capacity) {
        Node lru = tail.prev;
        removeNode(lru);
        map.remove(lru.key);  // that's why Node stores key!
    }
    // Case 3: Add new node
    Node newNode = new Node(key, value);
    addToHead(newNode);
    map.put(key, newNode);
}
5

Helpers — removeNode & addToHead

O(1) linked list ops

Remove: unlink node by connecting its neighbors

// Before: ... ↔ A ↔ node ↔ B ↔ ...
// After:  ... ↔ A ↔ B ↔ ...
private void removeNode(Node node) {
    node.prev.next = node.next;
    node.next.prev = node.prev;
}

Add to head: insert right after the dummy head

// Before: head ↔ X ↔ ...
// After:  head ↔ node ↔ X ↔ ...
private void addToHead(Node node) {
    node.next = head.next;
    node.prev = head;
    head.next.prev = node;
    head.next = node;
}

Common Follow-ups

Thread-safe LRU?

Use ReentrantReadWriteLock — read lock for get(), write lock for put(). Or use ConcurrentHashMap + synchronized linked list operations. Java's Collections.synchronizedMap(new LinkedHashMap(...)) is a quick shortcut but uses a global lock.

LRU with TTL?

Store a timestamp in each node. On get(), check if now - timestamp > TTL and treat as miss if expired. Background cleanup thread can scan periodically. Combine with this repo's TTLCache approach.

Distributed LRU?

Consistent hashing across multiple cache servers. Each server runs its own LRU. Client hashes the key to determine which server to query. Redis uses an approximation: sample N keys, evict the one with the oldest access time.

Why not just use LinkedHashMap?

LinkedHashMap(capacity, 0.75f, true) with removeEldestEntry() gives you LRU in ~5 lines. But interviewers want to see you build the doubly linked list + HashMap yourself to prove you understand the mechanics.

3

Edge Cases & Gotchas

Node stores key — When evicting from the tail, you need the key to remove the HashMap entry. Forgetting to store the key in the Node is the #1 bug.
Dummy sentinels — Without dummy head/tail, every add/remove needs null checks for edge cases (empty list, single element). Sentinels eliminate all of them.
Update existing key — put(key, newValue) when key exists must update the value AND move to head. Don't just update the value in place — that fails the "recently used" part.
